item.text: I’ll read the selected lyric, then reconstruct the source script verse by verse from the Roman transcription.

item.aggregated_output:
---
title: "Chaliya Ayn Te Akbar Watna Te Khairi Aawin Lyrics 2020"
language: "Urdu"
lang: "ur"
direction: "ltr"
kalamType: "Other"
poet: "Saqlain"
tags: ["noUrdu"]
aliases: []
published: false
---

1
Chaliya Ayn Te Akbar Watna Te Khairi Aawin.
Tere Rah Main Takney Roog Wichoray De Veer Na Lawin.
Bhain Haan Bhaijaan Gi Watna Taun Tere Nawein Veer Chithiyaan.
Mere Khat Jad Aaway Veran Ik Wari Seene Te Lawin.

2
Sham Aawaan Gi Phophi Zainab Kita Shereen Naal Wadah.
Tusi Sham Gaye Te Veer Na Mere Bin Sehra Sajawin.
Raat Din Veer Main Rowaan Gi Aidi Yaad Jad Sataya.
Mera Veer Asghar Nu Naal Madine Taun Moor Leyawin.

3
Ain Mumkin Aye Tere Badoon Mainu Maut Aa Sawaway.
Mainu Qabar Choon Aa Ke Shakal Wakhawan Layi Aap Jagawin.
Sain Saqlain Aye Kaindi Si Teri Karbala Taun Wari.
Jadon Shehar Wasawin Bhain Nu Aap Akbar Lain Layi Aawein.

/bin/bash -lc "python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p = Path(\"src/data/lyrics/chaliya-ayn-te-akbar-watna-te-khairi-aawin-lyrics-2020-tajpoints-773944ba4731751e6649.md\")
_, meta, body = p.read_text().split(\"---\", 2)
roman = meta.split(\"romanLyrics: |-\\n\")[1]
for content, numbers in [(roman, \"123\"), (body, \"۱۲۳\")]:
    blocks = content.strip().split(\"\\n\\n\")
    assert [len(block.splitlines()) for block in blocks] == [5, 5, 5]
    assert [block.splitlines()[0].strip() for block in blocks] == list(numbers)
assert 'lang: \"pa-Arab\"' in meta and 'direction: \"rtl\"' in meta
assert '\\u200c' not in body
print(\"Verified three numbered stanzas of four verses in both editions.\")
PY"

item.text:
Reconstructed all 12 verses in Shahmukhi Punjabi and preserved the Roman wording in `romanLyrics`. Punjabi grammar throughout the poem supports the updated language metadata. Verified that both versions have three matching four-verse stanzas.

I rendered the ambiguous Roman readings “Veran” and “Badoon” as ویراں and بدوں.
